metadata.title: Security Operations Authority SSPP
metadata.remarks: This SSPP defines authoritative decision, approval, and accountability boundaries for Security Operations (SecOps). It is the keystone SSPP on which all other SecOps SSPPs depend and explicitly prevents tool-, vendor-, or automation-driven authority drift.

import-profile.remarks: Instantiates the Security Operations composite and binds authority to its capabilities.

system-characteristics.system-description: Defines who may make security decisions, approve actions, enable or disable automation, accept operational risk, and own outcomes across Security Operations.

system-implementation.remarks: Authority within Security Operations is explicitly role-based and human-owned. No technology, platform, integration, or automation system may exercise authority unless expressly permitted by this SSPP.

roles.title: Security Operations Authority Owner
roles.remarks: Holds final authority over SecOps policy, decision boundaries, escalation rules, and approval of automation constraints.

roles.title: Security Operations Center Manager
roles.remarks: Operational owner responsible for day-to-day SOC execution within defined authority boundaries.

roles.title: Incident Commander
roles.remarks: Temporarily vested authority to coordinate containment, eradication, and recovery actions during declared incidents.

roles.title: Digital Forensics Authority
roles.remarks: Exclusive authority over evidence handling, forensic procedures, investigative methods, and chain-of-custody decisions.

roles.title: Security Automation (SOAR) Authority
roles.remarks: Authority to approve, revoke, suspend, or constrain security automation and playbooks.

control-implementation.description: Controls ensure that Security Operations authority is explicit, attributable, auditable, and revocable.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Incident response roles, responsibilities, and authorities are formally defined and assigned.
Security Operations personnel exercising authority are trained and approved prior to assuming decision roles.
Security Operations authority is documented and governed as part of organizational security planning.

statements.statement: Security monitoring systems, detection engines, analytics platforms, and dashboards SHALL NOT be granted authority to declare incidents or initiate response actions.
Automation (SOAR) SHALL NOT autonomously determine maliciousness, incident status, or risk acceptance.
All automated actions SHALL be attributable to a human-approved authority and fully auditable.
Digital forensics authority SHALL NOT be overridden or bypassed by incident response or automation activities.
No tool, vendor, service provider, or managed service SHALL inherit authority by virtue of access, integration, or configuration.

back-matter.remarks: All downstream SecOps SSPPs MUST reference this SSPP and SHALL NOT redefine authority independently.
